200.body: Polish opposition leader sparks controversy with speech on potential EU exit talks Oct 29, 2026 | Politics Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Jarosław Kaczyński, the leader of Poland’s largest opposition party, has sparked controversy by appearing to suggest that Poland and some other allied European Union member states could launch the process of leaving the EU if they fail in efforts to reform it. Kaczyński pomylił Krynicę z Kremlem. pic.twitter.com/tX0G04krze — Cezary Tomczyk (@CTomczyk) October 29, 2026 The comments in question came in an hour-long speech by Kaczyński at the Krynica Forum, an annual conference bringing together leaders from politics, business and civil society, which he used to outline his vision for sweeping reforms of the EU. The EU is preparing a "German plan" that would "annihilate the Polish state", said Kaczyński as Poland marks Independence Day.

300.title: Poland Inflation Eases in October
300.summary: News / Trading Economics / Poland Inflation Eases in October Poland Inflation Eases in October Less than 1 min read PLIRYY The annual inflation rate in Poland eased to 3.5% in October 2026, down from 4.1% in the previous month, preliminary estimates showed.
300.body: News / Trading Economics / Poland Inflation Eases in October Poland Inflation Eases in October Less than 1 min read PLIRYY The annual inflation rate in Poland eased to 3.5% in October 2026, down from 4.1% in the previous month, preliminary estimates showed. The slowdown was primarily driven by falling prices for food and non-alcoholic beverages, which declined by 0.1%. Meanwhile, costs remained elevated for fuels and lubricants for private means of transport, which climbed by 21.7%, while prices for electricity, gas, and other fuels rose by 6.0%. On a monthly basis, consumer prices fell by 0.4% in October, reversing a 0.7% increase in September and marking the first monthly decline after three consecutive months of growth.

600.title: Russian detained in Poland after photographing rail infrastructure
600.summary: Polish police said on Friday they had detained a 55-year-old Russian man suspected of acting for a foreign intelligence service, adding that a court had ordered him held for three months. Officers providing security for a football match in the southern Polish town of Swidnica spotted a man near a railway crossing photographing passing trains and railway infrastructure.
600.body: Polish police said on Friday they had detained a 55-year-old Russian man suspected of acting for a foreign intelligence service, adding that a court had ordered him held for three months. Officers providing security for a football match in the southern Polish town of Swidnica spotted a man near a railway crossing photographing passing trains and railway infrastructure. Police said they found thousands of photographs of key sites and transport facilities, not only in Poland, in his possession. Poland has repeatedly accused Russia of conducting espionage and influence operations on its territory, also using foreign nationals, while Moscow has denied such actions.
